standard.title: Criteria for Structural Design of Spillway Training Walls and Divide Walls (Second Revision) (स्पिलवे ट्रेनिंग वॉल्स और डिवाइड वॉल्स के स्ट्रक्चरल डिजाइन के मानदंड (दूसरा पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This standard specifies structural and hydraulic design criteria, load combinations, and stability requirements for both upstream and downstream training walls and divide walls in dam spillway and energy dissipator installations.
standard.scope: This standard specifies structural and hydraulic design criteria, load combinations, and stability requirements for both upstream and downstream training walls and divide walls in dam spillway and energy dissipator installations.

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this standard (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 12720:2004 is an engineering design standard rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its structural design, drainage layout, and stability check requirements is strictly mandated in public sector hydropower, dam, and river valley tender packages (issued by CWC, NHPC, SJVN, THDC, NEEPCO, and state irrigation departments) across India to guarantee safety against catastrophic hydraulic breaches and structural collapses. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Divide walls must be provided to separate bays having different energy dissipation arrangements (or different parameters/levels), or to allow for unsymmetrical operation of spillway gates to minimize cross-return flows, eddies, and erosion, as well as to isolate powerhouse bays or silt excluders.

Divide walls must be designed to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads caused by unsymmetrical flow in the energy dissipator. For flip buckets, hydrostatic loads must also incorporate centrifugal forces in addition to the depth of water, combined with corresponding full uplift on the wall base.

Under the non-discharging condition, divide walls must be designed for hydrostatic water pressure up to the minimum tailwater level on one side, combined with full uplift, active backfill pressures, or empty conditions on the other.

Requires masonry/concrete gravity walls where the strata above the foundation at the end or sides of the spillway consists of earth or poor rock. For sound, steep rock foundations, cantilever walls or thin concrete linings anchored to rock by steel dowels or rock bolts may be utilized.
Mandates integrating a comprehensive drainage system behind the walls (utilizing filters and drainage holes) in accordance with IS 11772 to relieve hydrostatic pressures and prevent piping failures.

The design of anchorages and reinforcement must satisfy the allowable stress limits specified in IS 456 (concrete) and the detailing provisions of SP 55 to prevent pull-out or failure of the wall base under peak lateral and uplift forces.

Enforces checking the structural stability of the walls against sliding (on soil/rock interfaces) and overturning, ensuring factors of safety comply with standard limits under both normal and unusual/seismic conditions.
